transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Redwood CSM), Ava Reynolds (CTO, Halcyon Forge), Dmitri Kozlov (Lead ML Eng), Maya Singh (Security Architect), Theo Park (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Halcyon is evaluating Redwood's API for prototypes, wants to understand time-to-first-token, how free credits & PLG quickstart work, and what it takes to move to Dedicated or Private with strict audit requirements. They asked about latency SLOs, prefix caching, K V cache behaviors, and encryption key management.

00:00 - Ethan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro—I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Sofia and Raj. How's everybody doing?
00:18 - Ava Reynolds: Good thanks. Excited to, uh, figure out the fastest path to get our ML features live.
00:30 - Sofia Martinez: Great, goal for today is to cover quickstart (free credits, TTFT), then high level infra choices — hosted, dedicated, private — and call out compliance items. We'll leave time for Qs.
01:02 - Dmitri Kozlov: Quick note from us: we have PII in prompts, and some completions will include customer data. We're sensitive to retention and residency. Also we're targeting 90 requests/sec at peak eventually.
01:20 - Maya Singh: And security side we're collecting vendor evidence for SOC2 and need to know about KMS and audit logs; we'll likely require encryption keys or bring-your-own.
01:35 - Ethan Chen: Absolutely. On the PLG path, most teams start with the Redwood hosted API using free credits to prototype. Time-to-first-token (TTFT) usually under an hour — sign up, get API keys, run simple generate/embedding calls. We'll send a quickstart guide.
02:05 - Theo Park: When you say free credits, is there a guardrail? Like 90 days, or usage cap?
02:13 - Raj Patel: Usually it's a fixed credit amount tied to the account you sign up with. For commercial pilots we can extend credits if you're actively running tests — we'll include that in the email.
02:40 - Ava Reynolds: Good. But for production we can't use shared multi-tenant hosting because of our auditors. What would Dedicated or Private look like?
03:00 - Sofia Martinez: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, single-tenant capacity with throughput guarantees. Private is a private control plane — VPC peering or on-prem option — where the inference plane sits inside your network. There's a slide in our security packet that shows network flows but we'll link it.
03:32 - Dmitri Kozlov: For Dedicated, how do you handle model variants? We may want smaller quantized models for cost savings and a big one for accuracy. Can you do automatic fallback?
03:45 - Sofia Martinez: Yes, our smart routing supports model variants by policy. You can route by latency or cost. Automatic fallback to a compatible variant is supported for resilience — if the high-perf model is busy we'll failover to a quantized one. There's some nuance around KV cache and cold-starts though — the K V cache warm-up can affect the first few tokens.
04:15 - Dmitri Kozlov: You said K V cash — I assume you mean KV cache?
04:20 - Sofia Martinez: Sorry, yes, KV cache. Transcription spell check aside.
04:30 - Maya Singh: For private deployment, can we manage KMS keys (BYOK)? We need explicit control.
04:36 - Ethan Chen: Yes, Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM integrations. We'll also provide audit logs with request-level metadata. Depending on the package, logs can be retained for a configurable window.
05:05 - Ava Reynolds: Latency is a big deal. Our product uses short prompts and expects <120ms p99 on simple completions. How realistic is that in Hosted?
05:20 - Sofia Martinez: Hosted can hit low latencies but p99 at <120ms is aggressive at scale. Dedicated with reserved capacity is the reliable path for tight p99 SLOs because you control capacity and tuning. Also batching helps throughput but increases tail latency — we can configure small batch sizes for low latency.
05:55 - Dmitri Kozlov: Any ballpark numbers for per-token cost between quantized smaller models and full 8-bit/16-bit?
06:05 - Raj Patel: We'll send a short cost matrix. Roughly quantized models can be 2-4x cheaper per token, varies by sequence length and batching. Our Optimize tooling will recommend quantization profiles per workload.
06:30 - Theo Park: For the quickstart, what does developer experience look like? SDKs, sample code?
06:38 - Ethan Chen: You get SDKs (Python/Node), OpenAPI-like endpoints, and sample prompt templates. Most teams are calling the REST generate or chat endpoints. We'll share a repo with a tiny demo app to spin up locally. TTFT is usually 20-60 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
07:05 - Ava Reynolds: Great. We want to run a small POC: 1) verify latency on our sample prompts, 2) check data handling and logs, 3) evaluate fallback policies. What's the recommended scope and duration?
07:20 - Sofia Martinez: A focused POC is typically 2 weeks: week1 self-serve with credits to validate integration and latency, week2 a short dedicated pilot where we provision reserved capacity for benchmark runs. We'll define success criteria together.
07:45 - Dmitri Kozlov: For benchmarks, do you provide a harness or should we supply prompts?
07:52 - Sofia Martinez: We'll supply a simple harness and can adapt it to your prompts. Action: we'll prepare a script that hits different sequence lengths and concurrency patterns.
08:10 - Maya Singh: Regarding compliance, can you provide SOC2 type II report and ISO documentation? Also SSO/SAML integration for our team access?
08:22 - Ethan Chen: Yes, SOC2 & ISO docs are standard; SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. For Private deployments we can offer more restrictive controls and longer log retention.
08:40 - Ava Reynolds: Any examples of customers in regulated spaces who've gone private or dedicated?
08:45 - Raj Patel: We have fintech and health customers on Dedicated and Private; we can share anonymized case studies.
09:00 - Theo Park: What's the lift on our side if we go Private on VPC? Network setup, peering?
09:08 - Sofia Martinez: Typically VPC peering plus a NAT and some routing rules. We'll provide a runbook. For on-prem it's heavier — packaging and ops support.
09:30 - Dmitri Kozlov: One concern: our current infra runs on a mix of cloud providers; latency needs to be low from our US-East region. Are there regions for Hosted?
09:42 - Ethan Chen: Yes, Hosted spans US-East, US-West, and EU regions. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions. We'll confirm latency profiles for US-East with the infra team.
10:05 - Ava Reynolds: If we start with self-serve quickstart and then move to Dedicated, what's the migration path?
10:15 - Sofia Martinez: It's designed to be smooth. You can pin model versions; when you commit to Dedicated we provision reserved capacity and update routing. We manage migration tooling and rollback policies.
10:35 - Dmitri Kozlov: For the POC, do you recommend using embeddings or the chat endpoint? We're doing retrieval-augmented generation, so embeddings plus a chat model.
10:45 - Sofia Martinez: That sounds typical. We'll recommend an embedding model profile and a chat/generation model; we'll also suggest prefix caching for repeated prompts to lower cost. Note: prefix caching effectiveness depends on prompt variance.
11:05 - Theo Park: Are there any quotas on the free credits that block automation tests?
11:12 - Raj Patel: Free credits are suitable for dev tests. If you need continuous integration load tests we'll temporarily bump credits or set up a short reserved pilot for testing.
11:30 - Ava Reynolds: Let's talk about success criteria for the pilot: p99 <120ms on sample short completions, no retention of PII in logs (or encrypted and access controlled), and cost target under our estimate — roughly $X per 1k requests. We'll finalize numbers offline.
12:00 - Sofia Martinez: Sounds good. We'll draft a short SOW for a two-week pilot with those three success metrics.
12:10 - Dmitri Kozlov: One more: can we run small A/B between quantized and non-quantized to measure quality delta?
12:18 - Sofia Martinez: Yes, A/B and rollouts are supported. We'll help set up evaluation harness and automated regression checks.
12:35 - Ethan Chen: Ok, next steps recap — we'll send: pricing matrix, SOC2 & architecture whitepaper, quickstart repo link, and a proposed pilot SOW. We'll also schedule a technical deep-dive to scope benchmarks.
13:00 - Ava Reynolds: When can we get the SOC2? We need it for our procurement asap.
13:05 - Ethan Chen: I'll attach it in the email today.
13:12 - Maya Singh: On the KMS/HSM question — we'll put together our BYOK requirements and send them over.
13:20 - Dmitri Kozlov: We'll also export a sample of our prompt distribution and payload sizes so you can recommend model choices.
13:30 - Raj Patel: Great, we'll coordinate calendar invites for the deep-dive.
13:45 - Theo Park: Anything else?
13:50 - Ava Reynolds: No, that's it. Thanks all.
14:00 - Ethan Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and action items.
